title: Tracks well, celebrates poorly
body:

When you complete a goal you've been working toward, the app should make you feel something - a proper animation, something visual, anything. The core tracking works fine but if you're trying to stay motivated long-term, the lack of a dopamine hit when you actually succeed is a real miss.

The widget also needs serious work. It refreshes with a noticeable delay and the icons don’t display properly. For something you’re supposed to glance at throughout the day, that’s frustrating. Has potential but these are basic things that should work.

title: Much better for people who don’t like routine!
body:
I really like this app. I’m basically running my life out of it now. 

I’m neurodivergent and I really hate routine. Previously I’d tried Tiimo but I couldn’t get into it for longer than a few weeks because it’s very time-consuming to plan out my whole day and then very awkward if I’m late with anything or plans need to change. It throws the whole day off. 

This app is very effortless. The reminders are very flexible and the motivation is very well-balanced: not too perfectionist, not too optimistic. I also find the record of tasks very helpful, and it gives me a happy to see everything I’ve done already. 

Only minor suggestions: it would be good if tasks could occasionally be deferred to the next day, if they’re not daily. Sometimes there are barriers to completion, like illness or weather, and if would be good to have the option to bump a task to another day rather than skip it entirely. 

Also, as someone else said, a little spray of confetti for certain key events (like getting a perfect day?) wouldn’t go amiss. It would be motivating to have that to aim for.

title: Apple Watch Needs work
body:
Going to preface this review by saying that a good Apple Watch integration with complications was a must for me when picking a habit app. On the surface Habitify meets the requirement. Good UI, useful iOS and watch apps, complication.

However the sync between the watch and phone and the complication update is atrocious. You complete something on the phone and it’s not there on the watch. You complete something the day before and the complication advances one step but does not reset after midnight, leaving you with one or more completed habits on the watch face that are not actually completed - shocking testing really. 

Have now switched to everyday, which was my runner up app, it’s not as nice but it’s at least functional.

title: No allowance for going beyond set goals
body: The only way to see every goal every day is to set your completion goal to 7 days a week. If my goal is to complete something five days a week but I manage to do it six (hooray!), it's very difficult log it (there is a way but it's fiddly and tedious). I spoke to the developers and was told they disagreed that it would be motivating to complete goals more often than the goal you set to begin with. Excuse me? Maybe some people prefer not to see completed goals in their daily list, but surely for lots of other people, seeing the things you've already completed is MORE motivational than only ever seeing all the things you still have left to do? Not to mention the good feeling that comes from being able to log an extra completion, going above and beyond your goal? Bottom line: this would be an INCREDIBLY easy setting option to add (no need to make it universal because sure, people have different preferences) but I was really appalled at the developers' suggestion that I obviously don't know what I find motivating. There is absolutely no good reason for not including this as a setting option other than sheer arrogance.

title: Another subscription app? Why?
body:
This is more of a general rant on pricing, but I’m fed up with apps that charge a subscription fee and don’t offer significant content worth subscribing to. 
This seems like a great app... I’d happily pay £20 for as a one-off. Maybe they could produce a new major version worth upgrading to some day, but an app which is basically local and just uses iCloud to sync my data to other platforms is not a “service”...my habits don’t need a rack of servers to justify ongoing fees. 
I don’t see what value could be significantly added to this app as it is to justify a commitment to pay for it into perpetuity...

title: Do Not Buy This App
body:
Let me say first of all that the app itself is excellent and very good at what it is supposed to do. 

However 2 days after I bought the app for 9.99 so not a cheap app, they informed us via their Facebook page that they were changing the pricing structure. 

As a consequence my 9.99 had merely bought a year subscription to what is in essence a tick box app 

It tracks habits, very low overhead, I doubt there is much more development that can be done yet they want to jump on the subscription bandwagon. 

At this rate every single app will go down the subscription model it is truly becoming insane. 

But in my opinion this was a dishonest move, they could have made it so that anyone who purchased after the introduction of the subscription had to pay it, as they would have signed up under those rules. 

So my advise to you would be consider streaks or some other habit forming app, as the only habit Habitify wants you to get into is paying their subscription.

title: Absolute life-saver
body:
I must have looked into at least 20 different habit apps while trying to put my life in order, and this one is definitely my favourite. That’s not to say it’s the unchallenged absolute best app out there, but it’s the best app for me, personally.

I’m a simple, private person. I don’t want social habit apps getting other people involved. I don’t want incredibly complex apps that have you enter every little detail. I don’t want a to-do list (already using TickTick for that). I just want an easy-to-use habit tracker that does its job and does it well. This one fits the bill perfectly.

It has all the usual features (custom repeats, reminders, etc.) but two in particular stand out:

- the ability to archive (and unarchive) habits. E.g. when you’re on hols and don’t need to water the plant every day, but don’t want to delete the habit and lose all your history or make it look like you left your plants to die for two weeks.

- categorising habits by time of day. I LOVE this. It’s even better because you can view the habits due now (e.g. this morning) or the habits for the whole day, and the latter list is still in chronological order. It’s almost like the app has a secondary function of being a planner while not being super detail-oriented or complex. Perfect, perfect feature.

Again, everyone has their own dream app. Yours might be something else. For me though, this is just right.

title: Highly recommend
body:
Thank you very much to the developers for the hard work they have put into this app. Not only is the app beautiful compared to some of its competitors, it is also highly functional. I especially enjoy the ‘time of day’ feature, which sorts habits into which part of the day they should take place. (The ability to repeat a habit a number of times a week as well as certain days is an honourable mention).

I have one idea that I would like to suggest the developers. This application would be even more powerful if you could ‘group’ certain habits together either through a tag or folder system. For example, I could tag ‘Study for Biology’ and ‘Study for Physics’ using a ‘school’ tag. This would make a noticeable difference in the usability of the app when you want to include many habits, as so far this app becomes less useful when more than a dozen or so habits have been added. 

I forgot to add the app uses a one time payment rather than a subscription for premium, which for me on its own was reason enough to use this app over many of its competitors. Please continue this policy devs!

author: Mr Bojman

title: good..BUT AVOID THE UPDATE/ be aware 14 day Journal Histogram GONE !!
body:
UPDATE:

Oh no ! The latest update REMOVED the 14 day journal trend histogram across the top of the page..

Downsides: 
-No instant display of last 2 weeks. This valuable feedback, destroyed by the update! 
-I now have to make an additional press to access prior days
-Redundancy: The current day feedback, a vertical line in place of the histogram DUPLICATES information already available  i.e. you can see your daily progress from the number of ticks. 

Response:
PLEASE REINSTATE THE JOURNAL HISTOGRAM (or provide an option to toggle on or off)

I had to remove a star for this change. Whereas I really would have liked to add one. This reflects the update making a major change to the app's visual feedback, that shrinks utility.

First impressions:

I've looked at other apps, and feel things are well thought out, with trends and 'streaks' clear and tangible. The price is definitely right, and I'll continue to use this app and update with observations accordingly.

I'm also happy to report the horrendous monthly fees of other developers are absent :-) As a result, I've paid for the upgrade. I definitely want to support the developers for their fair pricing.

Contrary to the other reviewer, I don't want the 'noise' of a multicolour application. It's distracting. In the long term, probably the best solution, is to provide themes.

It's still early days, but right I like what I see.
